body.name: I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}
body.construction:
Let \(m=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), discard observations with index larger than \(4m\), and put \(F_j=\{(j-1)m+1,\ldots,jm\}\), \(j=1,\ldots,4\).  Set
\[
 K_0(u)=\mathbf 1\{0\le u\le1\},\qquad
 H=\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}M},\qquad b=m^{-1/3},
\]
and, for \(V\in\{D,Y\}\), define the fixed-denominator contrast
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{j,h}^{V}(t)
 =\frac1{mh}\sum_{i\in F_j}V_i
 \left\{K_0\!\left(\frac{X_i-t}{h}\right)
 -K_0\!\left(\frac{t-X_i}{h}\right)\mathbf 1\{X_i<t\}\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal G_H=\left\{\frac14+\frac{kH}{64}:0\le k\le
 \left\lfloor\frac{32}{H}\right\rfloor\right\},
 \qquad N_H=|\mathcal G_H|,
\]
and retain
\[
 \mathcal A_H=\left\{t\in\mathcal G_H:
 \widehat\Delta_{1,H}^{D}(t)
 \ge\max_{q\in\mathcal G_H}\widehat\Delta_{1,H}^{D}(q)-\frac{\kappa_n}{8}\right\}.
\]
Write
\[
 B_H=\bigcup_{t\in\mathcal A_H}[t-H,t+H]\cap[1/4,3/4]
\]
and let \(\mathcal G_n(B_H)=(n^{-1}\mathbb Z)\cap B_H\), augmented, if necessary, by the two endpoints of every nonempty component of \(B_H\).  On this finite set define
\[
 \widehat c=\min\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{t\in\mathcal G_n(B_H)}
 \frac{\widehat\Delta_{2,H}^{D}(t)+\widehat\Delta_{3,H}^{D}(t)}2.
\]
If the displayed set is empty, set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\Theta\).  Otherwise put
\[
 \widehat y(\widehat c)=\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{Y}(\widehat c),
 \qquad \widehat d(\widehat c)=\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{D}(\widehat c),
\]
\[
 L_\alpha=\log(32/\alpha),\qquad
 R_c=\frac{2^{16}L_\alpha}{m\kappa_n^2}+\frac1n,
\]
and
\[
 r_n=8Mb+16\kappa_n\frac{R_c}{b}+16MR_c
       +8\sqrt{\frac{L_\alpha}{mb}}.
\]
If \(R_c>H/8\), \(r_n>\kappa_n/8\), or \(\widehat d(\widehat c)<\kappa_n/2\), set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\Theta\).  Otherwise let
\[
 A_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
 |\widehat y(\widehat c)-\vartheta\widehat d(\widehat c)|\le2r_n\right\}.
\]
Set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\operatorname{hull}(A_n)\) when \(A_n\ne\varnothing\), and otherwise set it equal to the singleton containing the projection of \(\widehat y(\widehat c)/\widehat d(\widehat c)\) onto \(\Theta\).  Smallest-argument tie breaking and the stated finite grids make this a measurable map of the sample.
